source: Test Heuristics Cheat Sheet by Elisabeth Hendrickson, James Lyndsay and Dale Emery. Descriptions are ours.

heuristics.name: Long input
heuristics.description: Text far longer than anyone would type can be cut off, overflow the layout or be refused without a message.
heuristics.apply: Paste a very long value (thousands of characters) into each text field and check what's stored and shown.

heuristics.name: Special characters
heuristics.description: Quotes, angle brackets, ampersands, slashes and line breaks often break display or storage.
heuristics.apply: Enter text with quotes, <, >, &, / and a line break, then check it comes back exactly as typed.

heuristics.name: Leading and trailing spaces
heuristics.description: Spaces around a value can make two equal values look different, or a required field look filled.
heuristics.apply: Enter a value with spaces before and after it, and a value of only spaces, and compare with the plain value.

heuristics.name: Wrong data type
heuristics.description: A field that expects one type (a number, a date) may accept or mishandle another.
heuristics.apply: Type letters into number fields, a number into a name field, and text into a date field.

heuristics.name: Number formats
heuristics.description: Numbers can be written many ways: decimals, commas, exponents, leading zeros, plus signs.
heuristics.apply: Try 1.5, 1,5, 1e3, 007, +5 and a very large number in numeric fields.

heuristics.name: Date edges
heuristics.description: Dates break at month ends, leap days, year changes and time zone switches.
heuristics.apply: Try 29 February in leap and non-leap years, 31 April, 31 December and a date around a daylight saving change.

heuristics.name: Far past and future dates
heuristics.description: Dates far from today can fall outside what the product expects to store or show.
heuristics.apply: Enter dates like year 1900, year 2100 and year 0001, and a date of birth in the future.

heuristics.name: Zero, one, many
heuristics.description: Code often handles none, exactly one and many items differently, and one of the three is wrong.
heuristics.apply: Try each list, cart or selection with no items, one item and many items.

heuristics.name: Create, read, update, delete
heuristics.description: Every kind of thing the product stores should survive being created, viewed, changed and removed.
heuristics.apply: For one kind of record, create it, view it, edit it, view it again, delete it, and check it's really gone.

heuristics.name: Follow the data
heuristics.description: A value entered in one place should arrive unchanged everywhere it's shown or used.
heuristics.apply: Enter a distinctive value, then find every screen, response or export where it should appear.

heuristics.name: Interruptions
heuristics.description: Stopping a task halfway (back, reload, closing, losing the connection) can leave data half saved.
heuristics.apply: Start a multi-step task and interrupt it: go back, reload, close the tab or cut the network, then return.

heuristics.name: Undo and go back
heuristics.description: Undo, cancel and the browser's back button should return to a consistent earlier state.
heuristics.apply: After each change, cancel or go back and check nothing half-applied remains.

heuristics.name: Repeat quickly
heuristics.description: Pressing a control again before the first press finishes can run the action twice.
heuristics.apply: Double-click submit, buy and save buttons, and press them again while the page is still loading.

heuristics.name: Some, none, all
heuristics.description: Choosing none, some or all of a set of options each exercises different code.
heuristics.apply: In checkbox groups, filters and bulk actions, select nothing, a few and everything.

heuristics.name: Starve the product
heuristics.description: Missing resources (network, disk, memory, a dependency) should give a clear error, not a hang or silent failure.
heuristics.apply: Slow down or cut the network, or make a dependency unavailable, then use the product.

heuristics.name: File size and type
heuristics.description: Uploads fail in different ways for empty, huge, wrongly named and wrongly typed files.
heuristics.apply: Upload an empty file, a very large one, one with the wrong extension and one whose content doesn't match its extension.

heuristics.name: Configuration variations
heuristics.description: Settings, preferences and environments change behaviour in ways few people test together.
heuristics.apply: Change each user setting (language, currency, display options) and redo a common task.

heuristics.name: Never and always
heuristics.description: Some things must never happen (data loss, a wrong charge) and some must always hold (a total equals its parts).
heuristics.apply: Write down the product's nevers and alwayses, then check each test result against them.

heuristics.name: Beginning, middle, end
heuristics.description: Items at the start and end of a list, text or sequence are handled by edge cases in the code.
heuristics.apply: Act on the first, a middle and the last item of each list, page and sequence.

heuristics.name: State transitions
heuristics.description: Things with a lifecycle (an order, an account) can be pushed into states or orders of steps the design didn't intend.
heuristics.apply: Draw the states something can be in, then try every transition, including ones that shouldn't be allowed.
